 Shantinagara, Bengaluru-27.
(BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-53-  F-0258)

(By Sri. M.S. Basavaraju, Advocate)
 SCCH-23 2 MVC No.700/2023  JUDGMENT
This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the M.V. Act, seeking compensation for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident.

2. The case of the petitioner in the nutshell is that, on 09.08.2022 at about 9.20 a.m., the petitioner was proceeding as pedestrian by observing all the traffic rules and regulations on Kanakapura Main road, near Jnana Sweekar School, Talagattapura, Bengaluru.

At that time, the driver of BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-53-F-0258 driven the same at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the passenger Auto and due to the accident the said Passenger Auto lost the control and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to the terrific impact the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries.

Ramya vs B.M.T.C on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90909796/
1

Immediately after the accident she was taken to Shankar Hospital and then to BGS GIMS hospital,
wherein she took treatment and she was discharged with an advice to regular follow-up treatment.
She has spent substantial amount towards medical and other incidental expenses.
It is specifically urged that, at the time of accident petitioner was working as Labour at BBMP and earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
It is specifically urged that, due to the said accident she lost her earning capacity and become disabled.
It is further urged that, the accident happened because of rash and negligent driving of the driver of the BMTC Bus.
Respondent being the Insurer cum owner of the bus, is liable to pay the compensation.
3. After service of notice, the respondent appeared before the Court and filed written statement specifically denying the petition averments.
This respondent contended that the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties.
This respondent denied the negligence of the driver of BMTC bus as the said bus in question was on its schedule trip from Nallakannapalya to K.R. Market.
The driver of the BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA- 53-F-0258 drive the same in slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road by observing all the traffic rules and regulations.

And while so proceeding on Kanakapura road in front of Janasweekar School, near Talaghattapura, at that point of time the Autorickshaw bearing Reg.No.KA-01-AD-2808 proceeding in front of the BMTC bus, who was driving the same in a rash and negligent manner and abruptly stopped the Auto without giving any signal or indication, consequently the driver of the bus in question also stopped the bus and in that process, it came contact with the Autorickshaw.
As such, for the alleged accident, the driver of the Autorickshaw was wholly and solely responsible but the driver of the Bus in question was no way responsible.
Rest of the averments of the petition are repudiated as false and baseless and it is prayed to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of the pleadings, the tribunal framed following issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that on 09.08.2022 at about 9.20 a.m., while she was proceeding as pedestrian near Jnana Sweekar School, Kanakapura Main road,
Talgatpura, Bengaluru City, at that time, the driver of BMTC Bus bearing Reg.No.KA-53-F- 0258 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the petitioner, as a result the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injury ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for ? If so, at what rate and from whom ?
3. What order or award?
5. The petitioner examined herself as PW.1. Ex's.P1 to 13 were marked on her behalf.
On the other hand Sri Nandeesh. H.N, the driver of BMTC Bus bearing No.KA-53-F-0258 was examined as RW.1.

Ramya vs B.M.T.C on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90909796/
2
6. Heard erudite counsel for the petitioner and respondent corporation on merits.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

7. This tribunal answers to the above issues are as follows :-
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3 : As per final order for the following :
REASONS 8. ISSUE NO.1 : The petitioner filed evidence affidavit reiterating petition averments.
Ex.P1 is the FIR registered by Kumaraswamy Layout Traffic police against the driver of BMTC bus bearing No.KA-53-F-0258 on the basis of FIS lodged by Chandrashekara Murthy.
N. Ex.
P6 is the wound certificate issued by BGS Global Hospital, Kengeri, Bengaluru, which indicates that the petitioner sustained injuries in a road traffic accident that occurred on 09.08.2022.

Spot mahazar Ex.P.4 &
Sketch Ex.P.5 corroborate the place of accident.

Ex . P7-IMV report discloses that the brake system of the BMTC bus was in order and the IMV Inspector has opined that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects of the said bus.
9.

Admittedly the accident occurred at the time when the petitioner herein was sweeping the garbage in front of Janasweekar School, at that time, the driver of BMTC bus bearing Reg.No.KA-53-F-0258 driven the same at a high speed in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the passenger Auto which is stopped in the said road in order to dropping passengers, and due to the accident the said Passenger Auto lost the control and dashed to the petitioner.
Therefore the BMTC bus driver did not have sufficient cause to cause the accident.

The fact that yet he went and dashed against the Auto and in turn the Autorickshaw dashed to the petitioner as she was sweeping the garbage leads to drawing of an inference that he was driving his vehicle rashly and negligently.
Hence the jurisdictional police have also filed charge sheet (Ex.P3) against him for the offences punishable under section's 279 & 338 of IPC.
There is nothing on record to believe that the charge sheet filed by the police is defective or collusive.
10. In the instant case there is no dispute with respect to the police documents produced by the petitioner which were prepared by the police while discharging official duty.
Said documents manifest that the accident in question had taken place purely due to the negligence on part of the BMTC bus driver.

It is noteworthy to state that the self serving statement of the driver of the offending bus (RW.1) cannot be attached any evidentary value as he would obviously give a different version of the accident to escape from the criminal liability which would in turn affect his employment prospects.
11. Moreover it is settled law

that the term 'rashness and negligence' has to be construed lightly while deciding a petition for claim of compensation under the M.V Act as compared to the word 'rashness and negligence' as finds mention in the IPC.
This is because the chapter in M.V Act dealing with compensation is a benevolent legislation and not a penal one.

Therefore, based on the above discussion I hold that the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the BMTC bus bearing Ramya vs B.M.T.C on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90909796/
3 Reg.No.KA-53-F-0258 is proved.

Accordingly this issue is answered in the 'Affirmative'.
12. ISSUE NO.2 :

As per the contents of the wound certificate the petitioner has sustained the following injuries : (i) lacerated wound over parieto - occipital region (ii) Abrasion over dorsal aspect of left elbow (iii) Abrasion over Left leg (iv) Abrasion over right knee.
It is needless to say that the injury No.1 is grievous in nature.
The Discharge / Dama / Transfer Out issued by BGS Global Hospital, Kengeri, Bengaluru indicates that the petitioner was treated as an outpatient.
13. The petitioner has deposed that on account of the accidental injuries she has become disabled and has lost her earning capacity.
However she has neither proved her avocation nor her earning capacity.
So also the petitioner has not examined the doctor or produced disability certificate to substantiate the fact that she has become permanently disabled.
Under such circumstances, it cannot be accepted that she has suffered permanent disability.
Therefore she is not entitled for compensation under the head 'Loss of future income due to disability'.
In this case the petitioner has produced medical bills as per Ex.P10 for having spent Rs.6,580/- towards medical expenses.
All these bills have been examined with care and are found to be correct.
It is pertinent to note that the petitioner in her cross examination categorically admitted that after the accident she was paid a sum of Rs.10,000/- by respondent corporation.
Anyhow because the petitioner has not proved that she has any kind of disability, compensation cannot be awarded under conventional heads.

Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the petitioner, the line of treatment and the medical expenses incurred by her, this tribunal is of the view that ends of justice would be met if the petitioner is awarded global compensation of Rs.60,000/-.
14.

The calculation table stands as follows :
Total compensation awarded : 60,000-00 Less interim compensation : 10,000-00 paid by respondent corporation Grand Total 50,000-00 15.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY :
Considering the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded, it would meet the ends of justice.
The Respondent being the RC owner/insurer of the BMTC bus bearing No.KA- 53-F-0258 is liable and directed to pay the compensation amount.

With this observation,
issue No.2 is answered as 'Partly in the affirmative'.
16.
ISSUE NO.3

: In view of the discussion made supra, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following :
ORDER

The petition filed under Section 166 of M.V. Act 1988, is hereby partly allowed with costs in the following terms :
The petitioner is entitled for global compensation of Rs.50,000/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire award amount.
Ramya vs B.M.T.C on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90909796/
4
The respondent is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
After deposit, the entire award amount together with interest, shall be released to the petitioner by way of E-payment on proper identification and confirmation.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw an award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer and printout taken by him, then corrected and pronounced by me in the open court on this the 9th day of January - 2025)
(Shreyansh Doddamani) XXI Addl. Small Causes Judge & ACJM, Bengaluru.
